For you, it may mean overthinking a decision until you can't make it, or judging more harshly than the situation deserves. Watch for power, including your own, being used unfairly. Being clever and being fair aren't the same thing, so check which one you're using.
sitWith: If you took the feelings out of it, what would the facts tell you? Whose expert advice would help you decide this fairly?
inASpread: Justice and the King of Swords together strongly suggest a legal matter or official decision. Beside the King of Cups, head and heart are working together. He ends a spread with a clear, fair decision based on facts. With the Emperor, rules, contracts, and authority weigh heavily.
imagery: A king sits on a stone throne facing straight ahead, holding a sword upright and slightly tilted, with butterflies carved into the throne and tall cypress trees behind him. He looks right at you, calm and serious, the judge who has heard everything.

waite.upright: Whatsoever arises out of the idea of judgment and all its connexions—power, command, authority, militant intelligence, law, offices of the crown, and so forth.
waite.reversed: Cruelty, perversity, barbarity, perfidy, evil intention.
waite.picture: He sits in judgment, holding the unsheathed sign of his suit. He recalls, of course, the conventional Symbol of Justice in the Trumps Major, and he may represent this virtue, but he is rather the power of life and death, in virtue of his office.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.meaning: Authority and judgment; Waite says he holds the unsheathed sign of his suit.
Air, thought, and change built into his seat of authority.
Clear, paired thinking: weighing both sides.
Steadiness and seriousness; decisions with lasting weight.

symbols.symbol: Cap of maintenance under the crown
symbols.meaning: Waite notes all four Kings wear it: responsibility of office.

history: Waite says this King sits in judgment and naturally recalls Justice among the trumps, though he is more the power of life and death that comes with high office. His meanings are power, command, authority, militant intelligence, law, and offices of the crown, and his extra notes call him a lawyer, senator, or doctor. In the Sola Busca pack this king is Alecxandro M., Alexander the Great himself.
numerologyAstrology: The King governs his element outwardly, and as Air of Air he is intellect in its purest form: analysis, law, and hard decisions.

upright.love: A partner who values honesty and fair dealing over drama. Love expressed through respect and straight talk. Anyone dating now may be drawn to someone steady and intelligent. Couples talk things through calmly and fairly.
upright.work: Leadership through expertise; lawyers, judges, doctors, analysts. Decisions should rest on evidence, whatever the mood in the room. Legal matters, contracts, and professional judgment go well. Rely on expertise and bring evidence to the meeting.
upright.money: Get professional advice, read contracts closely, and decide on the facts. Logic serves you better than hope. A financial adviser or a careful read of the fine print pays off. Decide on the numbers, then stick to the plan.
upright.advice: Think it through, then decide and stand by it. Fairness and clarity carry more weight than charm.
upright.asAPerson: Intelligent, principled, authoritative, sometimes emotionally reserved. He respects you and shows it through honesty. Principled, clear, and respected.

yesNo.why: A reasoned yes, grounded in the facts. A legal or official matter goes your way.

reversed.love: Coldness, control, or a partner who uses logic to dismiss feelings. Cruelty and evil intention are Waite's reversed meanings, so take coldness seriously. Arguments may turn into cross-examinations. Stand up for yourself calmly and look for outside support if it continues.
reversed.work: Abuse of authority, legal manipulation, or rigid bureaucracy. Keep records and get independent advice. An official could misuse authority or bend a rule for their own benefit. A lawsuit or formal complaint may be used as a threat.
reversed.money: Someone clever bending rules in their favor. Read every line before signing. A legal or financial expert may not have your best interests at heart. Get a second opinion before signing. Keep copies of everything you sign.
reversed.advice: Check your judgment for bias or pride. Use your intelligence to be fair rather than to win. Use power fairly.
reversed.asAPerson: Manipulative, cold, or tyrannical; the expert who uses knowledge as a weapon. His interest may come with control. Controlling, and hard to argue with.

yesNo.why: Judgment is being misused here. Someone may be bending the rules against you.

waiteNote.upright: Waite gives “whatsoever arises out of the idea of judgment and all its connexions”: power, command, authority, “militant intelligence” (a mind ready to fight), law, and “offices of the crown”, meaning government posts. In practice it's clear thinking, fair judgment, and professional expertise.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives cruelty, perversity, barbarity, perfidy (betrayal), and evil intention. In practice readers take it as intelligence used to control or harm, abuse of power, or cold, rigid judgment.

imageryHistory: The Marseille-pattern King of Swords is a crowned king seated with a sword. Smith sat him facing forward on a high throne carved with butterflies, his sword held upright and slightly tilted, with a few trees and clouds behind, and Waite says he recalls the figure of Justice in the Major Arcana.

mathers.title: King of Swords
mathers.upright: A Lawyer, a Man of Law, Power, Command, Superiority, Authority
mathers.reversed: A Wicked Man, Chagrin, Worry, Grief, Fear, Disturbance.
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Prince of the Chariot of the Winds
goldenDawn.printed: THE PRINCE OF THE CHARIOT OF THE WINDS
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: A lawyer, senator, doctor.
waiteAdditional.reversed: A bad man; also a caution to put an end to a ruinous lawsuit.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads a lawyer, a man of law, power, command, superiority, and authority, and reversed, a wicked man, chagrin, worry, grief, fear, and disturbance. Book T calls this court the Prince of the Chariot of the Winds.

name: Ace of Pentacles
upright: Something real is being offered. The Ace of Pentacles is a practical new start: a job offer, a raise, a business idea, a house, money coming in, or a chance to improve your health. Where the other Aces are sparks and feelings and ideas, this one is something you can hold in your hand. It's a seed, so it still needs planting and tending. Take the offer seriously and make a plan for it. Read the salary, hours, and terms before you sign. Put the first step in the calendar this week.
reversed: The opportunity is shaky or slipping away. A job offer might fall through, an investment might not be as sound as it looked, or you might be missing a chance because you're too worried about money to take it. Poor planning plays a part here, spending before the money is in, or building on weak ground. The timing may simply be wrong, and waiting is wiser. Check the details and the numbers before you commit. A good offer can still be the wrong fit. Look at what it would cost you in time and peace before you sign.
sitWith: What small, practical step would turn this chance into something real?
inASpread: The Ace of Pentacles with the Eight or Three of Pentacles points to a new job or training that could grow into a career. After the Five of Pentacles, it's a lifeline following a hard time with money. For anything to do with money, work, or building something, it's a very good card to finish on. Reversed near the Seven of Cups, a money idea may be more fantasy than plan.
imagery: A hand comes out of a cloud holding a large golden pentacle over a well-kept garden of white lilies, where a path leads through a hedge archway toward distant mountains. It's a real, solid gift, and the path suggests it's the start of something you can walk down.

waite.upright: Perfect contentment, felicity, ecstasy; also speedy intelligence; gold.
waite.reversed: The evil side of wealth, bad intelligence; also great riches. In any case it shews prosperity, comfortable material conditions, but whether these are of advantage to the possessor will depend on whether the card is reversed or not.
waite.picture: A hand—issuing, as usual, from a cloud—holds up a pentacle.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Hand from a cloud holding up a pentacle
symbols.meaning: A practical chance placed right in your palm, ready to be taken.
Growth that is tended with care and patience.
The way out of the safe garden into the wider world where the seed can grow.
Bigger goals the start could lead to, given years of work.
The pentagram, which Waite links to the four elements in human nature and what governs them.

history: In older packs this suit was coins, deniers in French, and the Marseille ace is one large ornamented coin with no hand at all. Waite wrote that he had not invented the change from coins to pentacles, and kept it because the cards do not deal especially with questions of money. His list of extra meanings calls this ace the most favourable of all cards.
numerologyAstrology: Aces count as one, the whole suit in a single seed. Root of the Powers of Earth is its Golden Dawn name, covering bodies, homes, money, and anything you can touch.

upright.love: A relationship finds solid footing: a partner who turns up when they say they will, or a real step like a lease signed together. For someone single, a meeting through work or daily routine can have staying power. Couples might buy furniture, open a joint account, or plan a home. It's a grounded, sensible start that grows with care.
upright.work: An offer with substance behind it, whether a job, a contract, a raise, or funding for an idea. Get the terms in writing and start laying groundwork straight away. Accept the training that comes with it, since skills compound over time. A mentor or a steady employer can turn this start into a career.
upright.money: Money arrives or a sound chance to earn it appears. Waite's list reads perfect contentment, felicity, and gold, so this is about as good as a money card gets. A windfall, a raise, or a new client could arrive. Open a separate account for it so it doesn't vanish into daily spending.
upright.advice: Treat the offer as a seed that needs a plan, a budget, and regular care. Small, boring steps taken early are what turn it into something. Plant the seed and water it.
upright.asAPerson: Steady, grounded, and generous with time as well as money. Their interest in you is practical and serious, shown in favors done more than in words. They'll plan dates you can afford and show up on time.

yesNo.why: Something real and useful is on offer. Solid ground points to yes.

reversed.love: Plans for a shared future keep getting talked about and never booked. Money worries, or one partner's reluctance to commit resources, can hold the whole thing in place. Fear about money can make a partner hold back on commitment. Talk about budgets openly so it doesn't become the silent reason for delays.
reversed.work: An offer falls through, or a project starts without enough funding to finish. Look hard at the numbers before you say yes to anything new. Check the details of an offer, like pay, hours, and security. It may be better to wait for a sounder opportunity.
reversed.money: Waite gives this reversal the evil side of wealth. Comfort may be there, yet it gets spent badly, chased greedily, or lost through a careless decision. Greed or haste can turn a good chance into a loss. Slow down and read the terms twice.
reversed.advice: Fix the foundations first. A smaller plan that you can actually fund beats a grand one built on hope. Look before you grab.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone who promises help and then can't or won't follow through, or who measures everything in cost. Their offers deserve a second look. Worried about money, or chasing it.

yesNo.why: The chance is shaky or slipping away as things stand. The opportunity isn't solid yet.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists perfect contentment, felicity (happiness), ecstasy, “speedy intelligence” (quick news or a quick mind), and gold. In practice it's a solid new start with money, work, a home, or health: something real you can hold.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives “the evil side of wealth” and bad intelligence (bad news), yet also great riches. He says the card always shows prosperity, and whether it helps the owner depends on the orientation. In practice readers take it as an opportunity delayed or wasted, or money that brings trouble with it.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Ace of Coins was a single large decorated coin. Book T describes an angelic hand holding a rose branch that bears a great pentacle of five circles, with a red cross at its center. Smith brought back the hand from the cloud holding up a single pentacle, over a garden of lilies with a hedge arch opening onto distant mountains.

mathers.title: Ace of Pentacles
mathers.reversed: Purse of Gold, Money, Gain, Help, Profit, Riches.
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Root of the Powers of the Earth
goldenDawn.printed: THE ROOT OF THE POWERS OF THE EARTH
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: The most favourable of all cards.
waiteAdditional.reversed: A share in the finding of treasure.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads perfect contentment, felicity, prosperity, and triumph, and reversed, purse of gold, money, gain, help, profit, and riches. Book T calls it the Root of the Powers of Earth, and Waite's additional note calls it the most favourable of all cards.

name: Two of Pentacles
upright: You've got a lot going on and you're handling it, just about. The Two of Pentacles is juggling: work and home, two jobs, bills and plans, all the things that need your attention at once. The young man in the card makes it look like a dance, and that's the trick here, staying flexible and light on your feet while the waves roll behind you. It's a busy card more than a bad one. Keep your sense of humor. Keeping two things going is a skill, and you're doing it. Leave a little slack in the schedule so one surprise doesn't knock everything over.
reversed: A few balls are about to drop. You've taken on more than you can manage, and something, maybe money, maybe sleep, maybe a relationship, is starting to suffer. Bills pile up, the calendar is a mess, and saying yes to everything has left you stretched thin. This can also be the moment you finally stop and decide what really matters. It's okay to put something down. Watch for missed payments and late fees, which are usually the first ball to fall.
sitWith: If you had to put one thing down right now, what would it be? What could you drop, delegate, or delay to make the juggling easier?
inASpread: If several Pentacles surround it, the juggling is mostly about money and work, keeping the bills and the hours in balance. Next to the Ten of Wands the act has turned into a crushing load, while Temperance nearby shows you finding a pace you can keep up. With the Knight of Wands, life is busy and changing fast.
imagery: A young man in a tall hat dances as he juggles two pentacles linked by a looping green ribbon shaped like an infinity sign, while behind him two ships ride high, rolling waves. He's keeping everything in the air and moving with the ups and downs.

waite.upright: On the one hand it is represented as a card of gaiety, recreation and its connexions, which is the subject of the design; but it is read also as news and messages in writing, as obstacles, agitation, trouble, embroilment.
waite.reversed: Enforced gaiety, simulated enjoyment, literal sense, handwriting, composition, letters of exchange.
waite.picture: A young man, in the act of dancing, has a pentacle in either hand, and they are joined by that endless cord which is like the number 8 reversed.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Young man dancing with a pentacle in each hand
symbols.meaning: Keeping two demands in play at once, and making it look like fun.

symbols.symbol: Endless cord looped around the coins
symbols.meaning: Waite compares it to the number 8 reversed, the sign of something kept moving without end.
A performer's touch, the showman keeping spirits up.

symbols.symbol: Two ships riding big waves behind him
symbols.meaning: The ups and downs of trade and life rolling on in the background.

history: In many Marseille packs the two coins sit inside an S-shaped band, which card-makers often used to print their own name. Smith turned that band into the juggler's looping cord. Waite gives the card two readings at once, gaiety and recreation on one side and news in writing, obstacles, and agitation on the other, and his extra notes add that troubles are more imaginary than real.
numerologyAstrology: Two is a pair to be balanced, and here the balance comes from motion. The Golden Dawn's Lord of Harmonious Change, it sits in Jupiter in Capricorn, growth that has to fit inside a tight frame.

upright.love: Fitting romance around work shifts, kids, or a long commute. It holds up well when both of you stay flexible and laugh about the chaos. Dating may mean fitting coffee between errands in a packed week. Keep plans simple and fun.
upright.work: Two jobs, several clients, or priorities that change daily. You're keeping up, so keep a running list and check it every morning. Flexibility is your strength right now, so use a simple list to keep track.
upright.money: Shifting money between accounts, covering one bill with another, or living on uneven income. It's manageable if you track it closely. Juggling bills works as long as you know the due dates. Put them all on one calendar and set reminders.
upright.advice: Stay light on your feet and decide what gets attention today. Handled is good enough for most of it.
upright.asAPerson: Adaptable, funny, and always busy. They like you and will fit you in, though their calendar is already crowded. They'll text back late, but they will text back.

yesNo.why: It can work if the balancing act holds. It could go either way depending on balance.

reversed.love: The relationship keeps getting bumped for other things, and dates are moved so often they stop happening. Enforced gaiety and simulated enjoyment, as Waite puts it, fit a couple putting on a cheerful face. Couples may be too busy for each other and pretending not to mind. Book time together like any other appointment.
reversed.work: Overcommitted and starting to drop things. A missed deadline is usually the signal to hand something off or turn something down. Something has to give before quality slips further. A second job taken on to cover bills may be wearing you down.
reversed.money: Late fees, overdrafts, and the strain of juggling bills with no margin. Write every payment down in one place and see what actually needs to go. Stop moving money around and look at the whole picture. A simple budget shows where the gap really is.
reversed.advice: Put one ball down on purpose before one falls on its own. The rest gets easier the moment you do.
reversed.asAPerson: Scattered, overbooked, and faking calm. They may care about you and still fail to show up on time. Overstretched and hiding it.

yesNo.why: Too much is in the air to give this proper attention.

waiteNote.upright: Waite gives two sides: gaiety and recreation, which the dancing figure shows, and also news and messages in writing, obstacles, agitation, trouble, and embroilment (getting tangled up in something). In practice it's juggling several demands at once and keeping them moving.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives “Enforced gaiety, simulated enjoyment”, meaning a cheerful face put on, along with the literal sense, handwriting, composition, and “letters of exchange” (bills or money orders). In practice readers take it as the juggling going wrong: too much on, money shuffled around, or pretending it's fine.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Two of Coins joined the two coins with a ribbon, often where the card maker printed a name and date, with no figures. Book T describes two pentacles joined by a green and gold serpent wound round them in a figure eight with its tail in its mouth. Smith drew a young man dancing with a pentacle in each hand, joined by an endless cord like a figure eight lying on its side, while ships ride high waves behind him.

mathers.title: Deuce of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Harmonious Change
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF HARMONIOUS CHANGE
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: Troubles are more imaginary than real.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads embarrassment, worry, and difficulties, and reversed, letter, missive, epistle, and message. Book T calls it the Lord of Harmonious Change, and Waite's additional note says the troubles are more imaginary than real.

name: Three of Pentacles
upright: Good work gets done together. The Three of Pentacles is teamwork and skill, people with different strengths working on something that matters. It often shows up when your work is being noticed, when you're learning a trade, or when a project needs everyone pulling in the same direction. The mason is good at what he does, and the others can see it. Speak up with your ideas, and listen to theirs. Asking for input makes the final piece better. Share the plan early and let people with other skills improve it.
reversed: The team isn't working. People may be pulling in different directions, someone isn't doing their share, or nobody's listening to anybody. Rushed, careless work shows up here, or not getting credit for what you did. Or you're trying to do everything alone when you could really use help. Get everyone on the same page before you build any further. Set clear roles and deadlines so nobody can coast.
sitWith: Who could help you do this better than you could do it alone?
inASpread: Paired with the Eight of Pentacles, this is a strong sign of skill growing through practice and training. With the Five of Wands nearby, the team has too many strong opinions and not enough agreement. Good results come from working with others if it's the outcome, along with credit for your part.
imagery: A young stonemason stands on a bench carving the arch of a cathedral, while a monk and a figure holding building plans stand below talking the work over with him. Each person brings something different, skill, vision, and purpose, and the building needs all three.

waite.upright: Métier, trade, skilled labour; usually, however, regarded as a card of nobility, aristocracy, renown, glory.
waite.reversed: Mediocrity, in work and otherwise, puerility, pettiness, weakness.
waite.picture: A sculptor at his work in a monastery. Compare the design which illustrates the Eight of Pentacles. The apprentice or amateur therein has received his reward and is now at work in earnest.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Craftsman on a bench carving the stonework
symbols.meaning: Real skill applied to real work, the apprentice from the Eight now at work in earnest.

symbols.symbol: Monk and a figure holding plans
symbols.meaning: The client and the designer consulting with the builder: three kinds of know-how on one job.

symbols.symbol: Three pentacles carved in the arch
symbols.meaning: Effort built into a lasting structure.
Work that serves something larger than the paycheck.

history: Waite describes a sculptor at work in a monastery and tells readers to compare the Eight of Pentacles, since the apprentice there has received his reward and is now at work in earnest. He lists métier, trade, and skilled labour, and adds that the card was usually taken as one of nobility, renown, and glory. Older decks showed three coins with no scene, so the church and the workmen are Smith's.
numerologyAstrology: Three is the first result of combining forces. Mars in Capricorn, drive harnessed to patient, skilled labor, is its decan, and Golden Dawn writers named it the Lord of Material Works.

upright.love: Building a life by working at it side by side, whether that means fixing up a home or planning a wedding. Respect for what each person brings is what makes it work. Love may start in a class, a club, or a volunteer project. Couples do well tackling a shared task.
upright.work: Your skill is noticed by people who matter. Collaboration with complementary talents goes well, and feedback from a boss or client is worth taking. Share credit generously, since good teams remember who did.
upright.money: Pay that reflects your expertise, or a group effort starting to earn. Spending on training or better tools pays back. A group investment or joint project can go well if everyone knows their share. Paying for quality workmanship saves money later.
upright.advice: Show what you can do and listen to the people planning the job. The best work here comes from combining crafts. Work with people who know things you don't.
upright.asAPerson: Skilled, conscientious, and proud of doing things properly. They admire competence and notice what you're good at. Skilled, humble, and a good team player.

yesNo.why: Good work and good teamwork carry this one. Others can see the quality of what you've done.

reversed.love: One partner carries the effort while the other coasts, and resentment builds over the imbalance. Talk about who does what before it hardens. Couples may argue about chores or who's putting in more. A clear list of shared tasks can take the heat out of it.
reversed.work: Mediocrity, pettiness, and weakness sum up the reversal in Waite's list. Sloppy work, a team pulling in different directions, or credit going to the wrong person all belong here. Push back politely on corner-cutting that you'll be blamed for later.
reversed.money: Paying for poor workmanship or losing money through a bad partner. Get quotes, check references, and don't pay the full amount upfront. Shoddy repairs and hired help who don't deliver are the risk here. Pay in stages as the work gets done.
reversed.advice: Raise your own standard and make roles clear. A good plan fixes more than extra effort does. Point out a flaw early, while it's cheap to fix.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone who cuts corners, won't cooperate, or cares more about looking busy than doing good work. They may leave the hard parts to you. Skilled but struggling with the team.

yesNo.why: The quality or teamwork isn't there yet. Fix the plan before you ask again.

waiteNote.upright: Waite gives métier (a trade or line of work), trade, and skilled labour, but says the card is usually read as nobility, aristocracy, renown, and glory. He links the sculptor to the apprentice in the Eight of Pentacles, who has now “received his reward”. In practice it's skilled teamwork and good work being recognized.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives mediocrity, “in work and otherwise”, puerility (childishness), pettiness, and weakness. In practice readers take it as poor teamwork, sloppy work, or skills that aren't being used or respected.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Three of Coins was an arrangement of three coins and foliage, with no figures. Book T describes a winged hand holding a rose branch with three pentacles in a triangle and two white rosebuds above. Smith drew a sculptor standing on a bench carving an arch in a church, while a monk and a figure in a patterned cloak hold up the plans, with three pentacles set into the stonework.

mathers.title: Three of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Material Works
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF MATERIAL WORKS
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: If for a man, celebrity for his eldest son.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads nobility, elevation, dignity, rank, and power, and reversed, children, sons, daughters, youths, and commencement. Book T calls it the Lord of Material Works, which fits the building in the picture.

name: Four of Pentacles
upright: Holding on tight. The Four of Pentacles is about money and security, and wanting to keep hold of both. Some of that is healthy: saving, budgeting, being careful after a hard stretch. But the man in this card is gripping so hard he can't do anything else, and that's the warning. Fear of losing what you have can make you stingy, controlling, or unable to enjoy any of it. Security matters, and so does room to breathe. Keep what you need and let a little flow.
reversed: The grip is changing, one way or another. You might finally be loosening up, spending on something you enjoy, being more generous, letting go of the need to control every detail. Or it swings too far the other way, into overspending or being careless with what you have. Sometimes it means holding on even tighter out of fear. Look honestly at whether your money is serving you or you're serving it. Generosity can feel risky after a hard stretch. Start with something small that costs you little.
sitWith: What are you holding on to out of fear, and what would happen if you loosened your grip?
inASpread: Next to the Five of Pentacles, it shows fear of going without driving the tight grip. With the Six of Pentacles, the lesson is about learning to give and share. In a love reading, especially beside the Two of Cups, it can point to someone who holds their heart the way he holds that coin, close and guarded.
imagery: A man in a crown sits on a stool hugging one pentacle tightly to his chest, with another balanced on his head and two more pinned under his feet, a city spread out behind him. He's so busy holding on that he can't move, can't reach out, and can't use any of it.

waite.upright: The surety of possessions, cleaving to that which one has, gift, legacy, inheritance.
waite.reversed: Suspense, delay, opposition.
waite.picture: A crowned figure, having a pentacle over his crown, clasps another with hands and arms; two pentacles are under his feet. He holds to that which he has.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Crowned man clasping a pentacle with both arms
symbols.meaning: Waite's own line is that he holds to that which he has.
Money sitting on top of every thought.
Planted so firmly on his wealth that he can't take a step.
Community and the wider world, shut out so he can guard his holdings.

history: Waite pictures a crowned figure with one pentacle over his crown, one clasped in his arms, and two under his feet. He reads it as the surety of possessions, cleaving to what one has, and also gift, legacy, and inheritance. In the Golden Dawn system it is the Lord of Earthly Power.
numerologyAstrology: Four is the stable square, and stability can set like concrete. Astrologically it is the Sun in Capricorn, where self-worth gets tied to rank and holdings.

upright.love: Guarding your heart so tightly that closeness can't get in, or a partner who treats you as a possession. Some security is healthy; jealousy is the warning sign. Singles may be protecting their heart after being hurt. Opening up a little at a time is enough.
upright.work: Holding on to your role, your budget, or your ideas rather than risk losing them. That keeps you safe but also keeps you from growing. Protect your role, yes, and let yourself learn something new too.
upright.money: Saving hard, protecting assets, and possibly an inheritance or legacy. Watch that careful doesn't become stingy with yourself and others. Savings grow and an inheritance or gift may arrive. Set aside some money for joy, too.
upright.advice: Decide what truly needs protecting and relax your grip on the rest. Money you're too scared to use isn't giving you much. Hold on, gently.
upright.asAPerson: Careful, controlling, and security-minded. They'll be loyal and protective, and may struggle to share or open up. Careful, protective, and hard to budge.

yesNo.why: You can keep what you have, though it may cost some freedom. Holding steady leans toward yes.

reversed.love: Waite gives suspense, delay, and opposition. A relationship stalls, or the tight grip slips and the fear of losing someone comes out in the open. Jealousy or possessiveness may come to the surface. Talk about what makes each of you feel secure.
reversed.work: Loosening up in a healthy way, or losing ground you tried to hold. Either way, the old defensive strategy isn't working. Delays and pushback slow a project down, so use the pause to plan. Hoarding information won't help anyone.
reversed.money: Swinging from tight saving to spending sprees, or losses that shake your sense of safety. Aim for a steady middle ground. Payments owed to you may be delayed or disputed. Plan one treat and stop there.
reversed.advice: Open your hand a little. Generosity and a bit of risk can bring more back than hoarding did. Find the middle ground.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone either learning to trust or swinging into recklessness. Watch which way they're going before relying on them. Swinging between stingy and spendthrift.

yesNo.why: Delays and opposition come first. Delay and opposition hold this up.

waiteNote.upright: Waite gives “The surety of possessions” (security in what you own), “cleaving to that which one has” (holding on), gift, legacy, and inheritance. He says the figure “holds to that which he has”. In practice it's saving, security, and a grip that can become too tight.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives suspense, delay, and opposition. In practice readers take it as the grip loosening, sometimes into overspending, or things held up and stuck.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Four of Coins was a plain arrangement of four coins with no figures. Book T describes a hand holding a rose branch with a single open white rose among four pentacles set in a square. Smith drew a crowned man seated with a pentacle on his crown, one clutched to his chest, and two under his feet, with a city behind him.

mathers.title: Four of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Earthly Power
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF EARTHLY POWER
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: For a bachelor, pleasant news from a lady.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads pleasure, gaiety, enjoyment, and satisfaction, and reversed, obstacles and hindrances. Book T calls it the Lord of Earthly Power, much closer to the controlling figure Smith painted.

name: Five of Pentacles
upright: Money is tight, or health is poor, and you feel left out in the cold. The Five of Pentacles is hardship of the practical kind: a job loss, a pile of bills, an illness, a winter where nothing seems to go right. There's loneliness in it too, the sense that you're struggling on your own while everyone else is warm inside. Look at the card again, though, because the lit window is right there and they're walking past it. Help is often nearer than it looks, like the lit window behind the beggars. Ask for it before things get worse.
reversed: You're starting to come in from the cold. This can mean recovering from a money setback, finding work, or feeling better after being ill. It often means finally accepting help you were too proud or too tired to ask for. A different kind of poverty may be the real issue, feeling lonely or empty inside even when the bills are paid. Winters end, and this one looks like it's starting to break. Accepting help is part of getting back on your feet.
sitWith: Where might help be waiting if you looked up from the snow? Where is the lit window you're walking past?
inASpread: Next to the Ten of Swords or the Tower, it points to a serious loss that will take time to recover from. When the Six of Pentacles or the Four of Wands sits beside it, help or a welcome is closer than it seems. If this card starts a spread and the Ace of Pentacles turns up later, a hard time with money is turning around. Beside the Four of Pentacles, fear of losing more may stop you accepting help.
imagery: Two ragged figures trudge through the snow past a lit stained glass church window, one on crutches with a bandaged head, the other barefoot and wrapped in a shawl. Help is right there behind the window, and they walk past without looking up.

waite.upright: The card foretells material trouble above all, whether in the form illustrated—that is, destitution—or otherwise. For some cartomancists, it is a card of love and lovers—wife, husband, friend, mistress; also concordance, affinities. These alternatives cannot be harmonized.
waite.reversed: Disorder, chaos, ruin, discord, profligacy.
waite.picture: Two mendicants in a snow-storm pass a lighted casement.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Two ragged figures trudging through snow
symbols.meaning: Waite's two mendicants: poverty, illness, and feeling left outside.

symbols.symbol: Man on crutches with a bandaged head
symbols.meaning: Health trouble piled on top of money trouble.
Warmth and help close at hand, and they walk past without looking up.
Hard conditions that feel as if they will never end.

history: Waite says this card foretells material trouble above all, matching its Golden Dawn title, the Lord of Material Trouble. He also notes that some cartomancers read it as a card of love and lovers, and admits frankly that the two readings cannot be harmonized. His extra meanings add troubles in love for the reversed card.
numerologyAstrology: Five breaks the safe square of four. Its decan is Mercury in Taurus, worry going round and round about money and the body.

upright.love: Hard times as a couple, or loneliness when you feel shut out. Waite mentions an older reading of lovers here, which suits two people getting through a lean winter together. Reach out to a friend, since company helps more than you expect.
upright.work: Job loss, reduced hours, or feeling excluded by colleagues. Help such as a union, a former boss, or a local program may be closer than you think. Look into benefits, retraining, or a former colleague who owes you a favor.
upright.money: Debt, a sudden bill, or not enough coming in. In its extreme form Waite calls it destitution, so ask for help early. Food banks, payment plans, and hardship programs exist for times like this. Call before the bill is overdue.
upright.advice: Look up at the lit window. Pride keeps a lot of people outside in the cold when someone would gladly let them in. There's no shame in needing help.
upright.asAPerson: Someone going through hardship who feels like an outsider. Their feeling toward you may be need, loyalty through trouble, or fear of being a burden. Struggling, and proud.

yesNo.why: Hardship stands in the way right now. Hard times say no for now.

reversed.love: Waite's reversed meanings run to disorder and discord, and his extra notes name troubles in love. Arguments about money or neglect can hit hardest here. Couples might finally talk openly about money or health worries. The relief of honesty can bring you closer.
reversed.work: Either coming in from the cold through a new job and a bit of support, or chaos made worse by denial. Ask for help rather than hoping it passes. Take the part-time job or the referral while you look for something better.
reversed.money: Recovery from a setback begins, or spending gets out of hand again. The difference is whether you face the numbers. Careless spending can undo a recovery, so keep a simple budget. Accept the help that's offered.
reversed.advice: Accept the help being offered and make a simple plan. Small, steady fixes beat one heroic gesture. Come in out of the cold.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone climbing out of a bad patch, or someone whose life is in disorder. Be kind, and be clear about limits. Recovering, and grateful.

yesNo.why: Things may be turning, but slowly. Help is closer, so it leans yes.

waiteNote.upright: Waite says the card “foretells material trouble above all”, whether destitution, as pictured, or otherwise. He notes that some card readers take it as love and lovers, wife, husband, friend, and affinities, and says “These alternatives cannot be harmonized.” In practice it's hardship, money trouble, illness, or feeling left out in the cold.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives disorder, chaos, ruin, discord, and profligacy (reckless spending or living). In practice readers take it as recovery beginning, or trouble made worse by denial or careless spending.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Five of Coins was a plain arrangement of coins with no figures. Book T describes a hand holding a rose branch whose roses are falling, leaving no buds behind. Smith painted two ragged figures in a snowstorm, one on crutches, passing below a lit stained glass window that holds five pentacles.

mathers.title: Five of Pentacles
mathers.upright: Lover or Mistress, Love, Sweetness, Affection, Pure and Chaste Love
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)
mathers.remarks: Shows simply that there is some one whom the person loves.

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Material Trouble
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF MATERIAL TROUBLE
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: Conquest of fortune by reason.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads lover or mistress, love, sweetness, affection, and pure and chaste love, and reversed, disgraceful love, imprudence, license, and profligacy. Book T calls it the Lord of Material Trouble, which is the reading Smith's picture follows.

name: Six of Pentacles
upright: Money is changing hands, and fairly. The Six of Pentacles is generosity and sharing: lending a friend what they need, getting help when you're short, a raise, a gift, a donation. You might be the merchant or the person kneeling, and life puts most of us in both spots at some point. The scales are there for a reason, since this is giving that's sensible and measured. When you have more than enough, pass some on, and when you need help, it's okay to take it. Fair exchange keeps everyone's dignity intact. Give what you can without keeping score.
reversed: The giving has strings attached. Someone may be helping you and then holding it over you, or you're giving so much that you're left short yourself. It can point to debt, loans that feel like leashes, or charity used as a way to stay in control. There's also the quieter side, being unable to accept help, or never giving anything to yourself. Ask who's holding the scales here and whether they're balanced. Notice who keeps the ledger and who owes whom.
sitWith: Are you more comfortable giving or receiving, and why? Are you giving and receiving in a way that feels fair?
inASpread: After the Five of Pentacles, the Six shows the help arriving. Next to the Four of Pentacles, it asks whether you can loosen your grip enough to share. Late in a spread, it points to support, a gift, or a fair exchange.
imagery: A well-dressed merchant holds balanced scales in one hand and drops coins into the open hand of a kneeling beggar, while a second beggar kneels beside, waiting. The scales say he's measuring what he gives, and the kneeling figures show who holds the power.

waite.upright: Presents, gifts, gratification; another account says attention, vigilance; now is the accepted time, present prosperity, etc.
waite.reversed: Desire, cupidity, envy, jealousy, illusion.
waite.picture: A person in the guise of a merchant weighs money in a pair of scales and distributes it to the needy and distressed. It is a testimony to his own success in life, as well as to his goodness of heart.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.meaning: Giving that is measured and fair, weighed before it's handed out.

symbols.symbol: Coins dropping into one outstretched hand
symbols.meaning: Help given where it's needed, and the gratitude of receiving.
Dependence and need, and the plain truth that anyone can end up on either side.
Enough resources to share around.

history: A person in the guise of a merchant weighs money in a pair of scales and gives it to the needy, and Waite calls it a testimony to his success as well as his goodness of heart. Presents, gifts, and gratification are the meanings, with another account giving attention and vigilance. Called the Lord of Material Success by the Golden Dawn, it also carries a warning in Waite's extra notes: the present must not be relied on.
numerologyAstrology: Six restores balance after the trouble of five. The Moon in Taurus is its decan, comfort and plenty that ebb and flow like a tide.

upright.love: Give and take that feels even. Kindness, gifts, and practical support flow both ways, or someone generous comes into your life. Couples share fairly and take care of each other in practical ways. Someone generous may catch your eye if you're single.
upright.work: A raise, a bonus, fair pay, or a mentor giving you a hand. You may be the one in a position to help someone else up. Mentoring, charity work, or a fair deal with a client goes well. Ask plainly for the raise you're owed, since the person holding the purse is open to it.
upright.money: Loans repaid, gifts received, or money shared wisely. Waite's phrase, now is the accepted time, suggests acting while conditions are good. Pay back what you owe and give within your means. A grant, loan, or gift may arrive at the right time.
upright.advice: Give what you can afford and accept help when you need it. Keep the scales in sight so generosity stays fair to you too. Share what you can.
upright.asAPerson: Generous, fair, and willing to help, sometimes a benefactor or mentor. Their care shows in what they do for you.

yesNo.why: Help and fair dealing are on your side. Generosity makes this a yes.

reversed.love: Gifts that come with strings, or one partner who holds the money and the power. Envy, jealousy, and illusion come up in the reversed meanings. Keeping score of who paid for dinner is a sign something is off. Talk about what each of you gives and expects.
reversed.work: Unequal pay, favors used as leverage, or a boss whose kindness feels like control. Know your worth before you accept an offer. Watch for favors used as leverage, and don't accept help that ties your hands.
reversed.money: Debt that feels like a leash, lending to someone who won't repay, or giving until you're short. Check the terms before money changes hands. Lending more than you can afford to lose leads to resentment. Set a clear limit and stick to it.
reversed.advice: Ask who is holding the scales and whether they're level. It's fine to say no or to refuse help that costs you your freedom. Notice who's keeping score.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone whose generosity comes with a hook, or who envies what you have. They may want more than they say. Generous with conditions attached.

yesNo.why: The exchange looks unequal right now. The exchange isn't fair yet.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists presents, gifts, and gratification, and another account gives attention and vigilance. He adds “now is the accepted time”, meaning the right moment, and present prosperity. In practice it's generosity, fair exchange, and help given or received.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives desire, cupidity (greed), envy, jealousy, and illusion. In practice readers take it as giving with strings, debts that feel like control, or help that's uneven.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Six of Coins was six coins among leafy ornament, with no figures. Book T describes a hand holding a rose branch whose white roses and buds each touch a pentacle, set in two columns of three. Smith drew a merchant holding scales in one hand and dropping coins into the hands of two kneeling beggars with the other.

mathers.title: Six of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Material Success
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF MATERIAL SUCCESS
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: The present must not be relied on.
waiteAdditional.reversed: A check on the Querent's ambition.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads presents, gifts, and gratification, and reversed, ambition, desire, passion, aim, and longing. Book T calls it the Lord of Material Success, and Waite's additional note warns that the present must not be relied on.

name: Seven of Pentacles
upright: You've been putting in the work, and now you're standing back to see what's grown. The Seven of Pentacles is the middle of a long effort: a savings plan, a business, a degree, a garden, a relationship you've invested in. The farmer isn't harvesting yet; he's checking progress and thinking about whether this is going the way he hoped. Good things tend to grow slowly, and this card asks for patience. It's also a fair moment to ask whether you're planting in the right field. Growth takes a season, and this is the middle of it. Measure progress against where you started.
reversed: The results aren't matching the effort. You may have worked hard for a long time and feel like you have little to show for it, which is truly discouraging. Impatience could be the problem, wanting the harvest before the crop is ready, or you've been pouring time and money into something that was never going to grow. Or you're about to give up right before things turn. Be honest about whether this needs more time or a different plan. Rethink the plan rather than working harder at a broken one.
sitWith: Is this something that needs more time, or something you need to stop feeding? What's actually grown from the work you've done, even if it's small?
inASpread: Alongside the Three of Wands, the Seven says the results you're waiting on are on their way. With the Eight of Cups nearby, the real question is whether to walk away from an investment that isn't paying off. The reward at the end is slow and steady, if you stay the course.
imagery: A farmer leans on his hoe and looks at a leafy bush heavy with seven pentacles, one more lying at his feet. He's done the planting and the work, and now he's pausing to see how the crop is coming along.

waite.upright: These are exceedingly contradictory; in the main, it is a card of money, business, barter; but one reading gives altercation, quarrel—and another innocence, ingenuity, purgation.
waite.reversed: Cause for anxiety regarding money which it may be proposed to lend.
waite.picture: A young man, leaning on his staff, looks intently at seven pentacles attached to a clump of greenery on his right; one would say that these were his treasures and that his heart was there.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Young man leaning on his hoe
symbols.meaning: A pause in hard work to take stock of what has grown.

symbols.symbol: Seven pentacles growing on a bush
symbols.meaning: Results ripening slowly, still not ready to pick.
What is already in hand compared with what is still on the vine.

symbols.symbol: His steady gaze at the crop
symbols.meaning: Waite says one would think these were his treasures and his heart was there.

history: A young man leans on his staff and looks intently at seven pentacles on a clump of greenery. He admits the traditional meanings are exceedingly contradictory: money, business, and barter, but also quarrel on one side and innocence, ingenuity, and purgation on the other. Golden Dawn tradition calls it the Lord of Success Unfulfilled.
numerologyAstrology: Seven is the point where you stop and reassess. Saturn in Taurus is its decan: slow growth that tests patience.

upright.love: A relationship that has had real effort and now needs honest assessment. Is it growing the way you hoped, or are you watering a plant that won't bloom? Couples may pause to ask where things are heading. If you're unattached, you might be investing slowly in a friendship that could become more.
upright.work: Mid-project, long-term effort showing modest results. Keep going if the plan is sound; adjust if it isn't. Take stock and keep going if the numbers look reasonable. Small course corrections now save a lot of wasted effort later.
upright.money: Investments or savings growing slowly. Waite's core reading is money, business, and barter, so look at returns with a clear head. Pensions and long-term savings plans fit this card. Give them time before you judge them.
upright.advice: Step back, measure progress honestly, and decide whether to keep tending or plant something else. Patience only helps if the crop is worth it. Be patient with the harvest.
upright.asAPerson: Patient, thoughtful, and invested for the long haul. They may be weighing what the relationship gives back for what they've put in.

yesNo.why: Growth is real but slow. It's too early to know.

reversed.love: Effort without results, or impatience with how long love takes to grow. One person may feel they've given far more than they've received. Impatience can cut something short that just needed time. Talk about expectations openly.
reversed.work: Hard work that hasn't paid off, or giving up just before it does. Rethink the strategy before you quit altogether. Burnout may come from effort without reward, so change the approach before you quit. Ask for feedback on what's not working.
reversed.money: Waite's reversed meaning is cause for anxiety regarding money which it may be proposed to lend. Be wary of loans and poor returns. Think twice before lending money or putting more into a failing investment. Cut your losses if the numbers say so.
reversed.advice: Be honest about whether this crop can grow at all. If it can't, cut your losses; if it can, stop pulling it up to check the roots. Keep the goal and change the plan.
reversed.asAPerson: Frustrated, impatient, or ready to walk away. They may feel their efforts aren't being rewarded. Discouraged, and working too hard.

yesNo.why: Returns look poor for the effort so far. The effort isn't paying off yet.

waiteNote.upright: Waite calls the meanings “exceedingly contradictory”. In the main it's money, business, and barter, but one reading gives altercation and quarrel, another innocence, ingenuity, and purgation (clearing out). In practice it's patience with a long effort, checking what's grown.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives “Cause for anxiety regarding money which it may be proposed to lend”, a worry about a loan. In practice readers take it as effort that isn't paying off, impatience, or a bad investment of time or money.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Seven of Coins was seven coins among ornament, with no figures. Book T describes seven pentacles with only five rosebuds that hang over them without touching. Smith drew a young farmer leaning on his hoe and gazing at seven pentacles growing on a green bush, as if weighing whether the harvest was worth the work.

mathers.title: Seven of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)
mathers.remarks: R. The next card will show the reason of the anxiety, and so on.

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Success Unfulfilled
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF SUCCESS UNFULFILLED
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: Improved position for a lady's future husband.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads money, finance, treasure, gain, and profit, and reversed, disturbance, worry, anxiety, and melancholy. Book T calls it the Lord of Success Unfulfilled, which matches the waiting in the picture.

name: Eight of Pentacles
upright: The Eight of Pentacles is practice, the slow, unglamorous way anyone gets good at anything. The craftsman is making the same pentacle again and again, and each one is a little better than the last. It shows up when you're learning a trade, training for a job, studying, or putting hours into a craft you care about. Nobody is watching and nobody is clapping, and that's fine. The skill you're building now will still be yours years from now. Doing the same thing well, over and over, is how mastery happens. Keep your focus on the next piece.
reversed: The work has lost its point. You may be stuck in a job with no room to grow, repeating the same tasks without getting any better, or bored stiff with something you used to love. Perfectionism can creep in too, redoing the same piece so many times it never gets finished. The other side is cutting corners and turning in sloppy work because you've stopped caring. Ask whether you need a new challenge or a new craft altogether. Ask yourself whether the work still teaches you anything.
sitWith: What skill would you be glad, a year from now, that you practiced today?
inASpread: Paired with the Three of Pentacles, the Eight points to training, an apprenticeship, or a job where your skill will be noticed. Among lots of Swords, it can be work used as a way to stop thinking about something painful. In the outcome spot, the steady effort pays off. With the Three of Pentacles, your practice is ready to be seen.
imagery: A craftsman sits at his bench hammering a design into a pentacle, with six finished ones hung on a post beside him and one more at his feet, a town far off in the distance. He's head down and focused, turning out one careful piece after another.

waite.upright: Work, employment, commission, craftsmanship, skill in craft and business, perhaps in the preparatory stage.
waite.reversed: Voided ambition, vanity, cupidity, exaction, usury. It may also signify the possession of skill, in the sense of the ingenious mind turned to cunning and intrigue.
waite.picture: An artist in stone at his work, which he exhibits in the form of trophies.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Craftsman bent over his bench with a hammer and chisel
symbols.meaning: Focused, repeated practice that builds real skill.

symbols.symbol: Finished pentacles hung on a post like trophies
symbols.meaning: Work put on display, each piece a little better than the last.

symbols.symbol: Town far off in the background
symbols.meaning: The world and its distractions kept at arm's length while he works.
Real, dirty-hands labor done for a living.

history: An artist in stone at his work, which he exhibits in the form of trophies, is the whole of Waite's description. Work, employment, commission, and craftsmanship, perhaps in the preparatory stage, are the meanings, which is why Waite later calls the sculptor of the Three the same apprentice now at work in earnest. The Lord of Prudence, its Golden Dawn title, fits that patient stage.
numerologyAstrology: Eight is steady effort toward mastery. Golden Dawn astrologers put it at the Sun in Virgo: attention to detail and quiet pride in useful work.

upright.love: Love built through small daily care: remembering the little things, fixing what's broken, showing up on the ordinary days. It may not be dramatic, and it is dependable. Couples may be building something practical together, like a home. Romance may grow out of work or study.
upright.work: Training, an apprenticeship, a new course, or long hours perfecting a craft. Nobody's applauding yet, and the skill you're building will outlast any praise. A qualification or certificate may be worth getting now. Good work gets noticed.
upright.money: Earnings from diligence, overtime, or a trade you're good at. Waite includes commission and skill in business, so steady, well-made work pays. Steady earnings from skilled work add up. Invest in tools or training.
upright.advice: Put your head down and practice one piece at a time. Each attempt makes the next one better. Keep practicing.
upright.asAPerson: Diligent, focused, quietly skilled, often a little absorbed in their work. They show affection through reliability and effort more than words. Hardworking and focused.

yesNo.why: Steady work gets you there. Effort pays off here.

reversed.love: All routine and no heart, or a partner so absorbed in work that the relationship gets the leftovers. Ask for time that isn't about chores or schedules. Chores done grudgingly or carelessly can start fights. Put the tools down for an evening.
reversed.work: Waite's reversed reading is voided ambition and vanity, along with skill turned to cunning and intrigue. Boredom, sloppy shortcuts, or endless perfectionism can all stall the job. Perfectionism may be slowing you down, or the work may have stopped feeling meaningful. Take a step back and ask what you want from it.
reversed.money: Working hard without getting ahead, or cleverness used for shady ends. Check that your effort is being paid fairly, and be wary of anyone offering an angle. Watch for high interest on loans and anyone charging more than is fair. Read the terms closely.
reversed.advice: Ask whether you need a new challenge or simply a higher standard. Repeating the same mistake isn't practice. Find the purpose again.
reversed.asAPerson: Bored and going through the motions, or clever in a way that bends rules. Skill and trustworthiness don't always come together. Driven, and sometimes cutting corners.

yesNo.why: The work has lost its direction. Sloppy work now leads to no.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists work, employment, commission (a paid job or order), craftsmanship, and skill in craft and business, “perhaps in the preparatory stage”, meaning still learning. In practice it's practice, diligence, and getting better at something through repetition.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives voided ambition (ambition gone empty), vanity, cupidity (greed), exaction (demanding too much), and usury (charging unfair interest). He adds that it can mean skill turned to “cunning and intrigue”. In practice readers take it as work without purpose, perfectionism, or cleverness used badly.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Eight of Coins was a plain arrangement of eight coins with no figures. Book T describes a hand holding a rose branch whose four roses touch only the lower four pentacles. Smith drew a craftsman at his bench carving pentacles, with the finished ones hung on a post beside him and a town in the distance, the artist in stone Waite describes.

mathers.title: Eight of Pentacles
mathers.upright: A dark Girl, Beauty, Candour, Chastity, Innocence, Modesty
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Prudence
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF PRUDENCE
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: A young man in business who has relations with the Querent; a dark girl.
waiteAdditional.reversed: The Querent will be compromised in a matter of money-lending.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads a dark girl, beauty, candour, chastity, innocence, and modesty, and reversed, flattery, usury, hypocrisy, and shifty. Book T calls it the Lord of Prudence, careful work over quick gain.

name: Nine of Pentacles
upright: She did this herself. The Nine of Pentacles is comfort and independence that you earned: a home you love, money put aside, the freedom to spend an afternoon in the garden because the work is done. It's about self-reliance and being happy in your own company, not needing anyone else to provide. The falcon on her glove is hooded and calm, a sign of discipline that paid off. You're allowed to enjoy what you've built. You worked for this.
reversed: The comfort has a crack in it. Working so hard to get ahead can mean you never get to enjoy the garden, or you're spending to look successful rather than to be happy. Money setbacks fit here, living beyond your means, or leaning on someone else's money in a way that costs you your freedom. Sometimes it's independence gone too far, so self-sufficient that nobody gets in. Think about what security really means to you. Check that the comfort is really yours and not borrowed.
sitWith: What have you built that you haven't stopped to enjoy?
inASpread: The Nine of Cups next to it makes a doubly contented picture, the wish and the means both in hand. Near the Two of Cups or the Lovers, it can raise a real question about how to share a life you've built so carefully on your own. Drawn as the outcome, it means financial independence and a well-earned rest. With the Queen of Pentacles, comfort and generosity go hand in hand.
imagery: A woman in a gown covered with flowers stands alone in a lush vineyard, a hooded falcon perched on her gloved hand, with ripe grapes and nine pentacles all around her and a snail at her feet. She earned all of this herself and she's comfortable enjoying it on her own.

waite.upright: Prudence, safety, success, accomplishment, certitude, discernment.
waite.reversed: Roguery, deception, voided project, bad faith.
waite.picture: A woman, with a bird upon her wrist, stands amidst a great abundance of grapevines in the garden of a manorial house. It is a wide domain, suggesting plenty in all things. Possibly it is her own possession and testifies to material well-being.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Woman in a robe patterned with Venus symbols
symbols.meaning: Comfort, beauty, and pleasure that she earned herself.

symbols.symbol: Hooded falcon on her gloved hand
symbols.meaning: Discipline and self-control that paid off.
Plenty in all things, as Waite puts it, ripe for the picking.
Possibly her own possession, a sign of material well-being.

symbols.symbol: Snail on the ground at her feet
symbols.meaning: Slow, steady progress over years.

history: A woman with a bird upon her wrist stands among grapevines in the garden of a manorial house, and Waite adds that possibly it is her own possession and testifies to material well-being. Prudence, safety, success, accomplishment, and discernment make up the list of meanings. Book T names it the Lord of Material Gain.
numerologyAstrology: Nine is close to completion and comfortable there. Venus in Virgo rules its decan: beauty and pleasure earned through practical care.

upright.love: Happy in your own company, or a relationship where both people keep their independence. A partner here is a choice you make, and you'd feel whole without one. Being single feels comfortable, with no rush to change it. A partner may admire how capable you are.
upright.work: Success earned over years, self-employment, or a role where you're trusted to run things. Waite's discernment and certitude fit someone who knows exactly what they're worth. Enjoy the rewards of years of work.
upright.money: Financial independence, savings that let you breathe, and a home or garden you enjoy. Spend a little on something beautiful, because you've earned it. A home you own or a garden you've made is the reward on show here. Treat yourself to something lasting.
upright.advice: Enjoy what you've built without apologizing for it. Self-reliance is a strength worth protecting.
upright.asAPerson: Self-made, refined, independent, and good company. They're attracted to you and won't give up their freedom for anyone. They like nice things and have paid for them themselves.

yesNo.why: Your own work has made this possible. Earned comfort says yes.

reversed.love: Independence that has hardened into loneliness, or staying with someone mainly for the comfort they provide. Deception and bad faith are in Waite's reversed list, so check what's really being offered. Staying in a relationship for security can leave you lonely inside it. Be honest with yourself about why you stay.
reversed.work: A project that comes to nothing, which Waite calls a voided project, or success built on borrowed credibility. Make sure your security rests on your own work. A project may fall through, or someone may not be dealing honestly. Keep your own records.
reversed.money: Living beyond your means, or leaning on someone else's money in a way that costs your freedom. Look honestly at who pays for what. Spending to look successful drains real security. Cut back on appearances.
reversed.advice: Ask what security really means to you. Comfort that depends on someone else isn't the same as independence. Build on your own ground.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone who looks prosperous and may be pretending, or who can't let anyone close. Waite even says roguery, so be careful with their promises. Comfortable on the outside, uneasy within.

yesNo.why: The comfort may be less solid than it looks. The foundation isn't solid.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists prudence, safety, success, accomplishment, certitude (confidence), and discernment (good judgment). He describes the garden as possibly the woman's own, a sign of material well-being. In practice it's independence and comfort that you've earned.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives roguery (dishonest behavior), deception, “voided project” (a plan that comes to nothing), and bad faith. In practice readers take it as comfort built on shaky ground, overspending to look successful, or dependence.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Nine of Coins was nine coins and ornament, with no figures. Book T describes a hand holding a rose branch with nine white roses, each touching a pentacle. Smith drew a richly dressed woman in a vineyard with a hooded falcon on her gloved hand, a snail at her feet, and a manor house behind her.

mathers.title: Nine of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Material Gain
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF MATERIAL GAIN
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: Prompt fulfilment of what is presaged by neighbouring cards.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads discretion, circumspection, prudence, and discernment, and reversed, deceit, bad faith, artifices, and deception. Book T calls it the Lord of Material Gain, and Mathers and Waite line up closely on this card.

name: Ten of Pentacles
upright: This is wealth that outlasts a single lifetime. The Ten of Pentacles is family money, inheritance, a house that stays in the family, a business passed from parent to child, the long-term security that comes from building slowly and well. The old man at the archway has seen it all come together, and the child will carry it on. Settling down belongs here too, buying a home, or making choices with the next generation in mind. Put simply, it's a card about roots. Think about what you'd like to pass on, in money and in values. Long-term choices matter here.
reversed: Money and family are getting tangled. There may be arguments over an inheritance, a will, or who gets what, or strain in a family business. Financial loss is possible, debts handed down, or a family that looks prosperous while falling apart underneath. Tradition can weigh heavy here too, with expectations about the right career or marriage that don't fit you. Think about what you really want to pass on, and what you'd rather let end with you. Watch for a relative who uses money as leverage.
sitWith: What do you want to leave behind for the people who come after you?
inASpread: Alongside the Ten of Cups, you get the full picture of a happy, secure family life. With the Five of Wands or the Five of Swords, it points to family conflict, often over money or property. It ends a reading with stability that's built to be handed down. With the Four of Pentacles, family money may be tightly held.
imagery: An old man in a patterned robe sits by an archway petting two white dogs, while a young couple and a child stand nearby, a family crest hangs on the wall, and ten pentacles float over everything in the shape of the Tree of Life. Three generations share one home, and the wealth here is meant to last.

waite.upright: Gain, riches; family matters, archives, extraction, the abode of a family.
waite.reversed: Chance, fatality, loss, robbery, games of hazard; sometimes gift, dowry, pension.
waite.picture: A man and woman beneath an archway which gives entrance to a house and domain. They are accompanied by a child, who looks curiously at two dogs accosting an ancient personage seated in the foreground. The child's hand is on one of them.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Old man seated in the foreground with two dogs
symbols.meaning: The ancient personage: the elder who built the family's security.

symbols.symbol: Couple under the archway with a child
symbols.meaning: Three generations together, wealth that lasts.

symbols.symbol: Coat of arms on the arch
symbols.meaning: Family name, lineage, and what gets handed down.

symbols.symbol: Ten pentacles set out in the Tree of Life pattern
symbols.meaning: Completeness in the material world, arranged in a Kabbalistic order.

symbols.symbol: Child's hand resting on one of the dogs
symbols.meaning: Loyalty and continuity carried on to the next generation.

history: Under an archway leading to a house and domain stand a man and woman, with a child looking curiously at two dogs and an ancient personage seated in the foreground. Gain, riches, family matters, archives, extraction, and the abode of a family are what it signifies. It carries the title Lord of Wealth in the Golden Dawn system.
numerologyAstrology: Ten closes the cycle, and here the completion is material and lasting. Mercury in Virgo is the decan: careful management of what's been built.

upright.love: Commitment meant to last: marriage, a family home, or a partner who fits in with your relatives. Love that turns into a legacy. An introduction through family or old friends may lead somewhere. Couples plan for the long term, including children or a home.
upright.work: A family business, a stable career with real security, or long-term plans finally paying off. Think in decades rather than quarters. Stability and long-term prospects are good now. Build something that lasts.
upright.money: Inheritance, property, family wealth, or long-term investments maturing. Waite's gain and riches, with archives and family matters, point to wills, trusts, and paperwork too. Wills, trusts, and property deals go well. Keep the paperwork in order.
upright.advice: Build for the long term and honor where you came from. What you set up now can outlast you. Plan for the long run.
upright.asAPerson: Rooted, family-minded, and established. They picture a future with you that includes both your families and a home. They take tradition seriously, from holidays to family recipes.

yesNo.why: Long-term security favors this. Lasting security says yes.

reversed.love: Family disapproval, pressure to settle down the approved way, or arguments over money and inheritance. Loss and fatality are among Waite's reversed meanings, so the stakes can feel high. A partner's family may see you as an outsider. Set boundaries with relatives kindly and clearly.
reversed.work: A family business in trouble, or a career chosen to please relatives. Ask what you genuinely want to pass on. Redundancies or a takeover may hit a job that everyone assumed was safe for life. Have a backup plan.
reversed.money: Loss, disputes over a will, or gambling with security. Waite also lists gift, dowry, and pension, so a family payout may come with strings. Avoid gambling or risky bets with family money. Get a will or agreement in writing to prevent disputes.
reversed.advice: Separate what you owe your family from what you owe yourself. Protect what matters before it's squandered.
reversed.asAPerson: Someone weighed down by family expectations or family money. Expect them to feel pulled between you and their people.

yesNo.why: Family or money trouble gets in the way. Get outside advice before anything is signed.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists gain, riches, family matters, archives (records), extraction (lineage or descent), and “the abode of a family”, meaning the family home. In practice it's lasting wealth, family, and security that passes between generations.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives chance, fatality, loss, robbery, and “games of hazard” (gambling), and sometimes gift, dowry, or pension. In practice readers take it as family money trouble, disputes over an inheritance, or security put at risk.

imageryHistory: In Marseille-pattern decks the Ten of Coins was a plain arrangement of ten coins with no figures. Book T describes a hand holding a branch whose roses touch all ten pentacles, with no buds.
