Smith drew an old man in a patterned cloak with two dogs, and a couple and child beneath an archway into a town, with the ten pentacles laid over the scene in the pattern of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.

mathers.title: Ten of Pentacles
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of Wealth
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF WEALTH
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: Represents house or dwelling, and derives its value from other cards.
waiteAdditional.reversed: An occasion which may be fortunate or otherwise.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads house, dwelling, habitation, and family, and reversed, gambling, dissipation, robbery, and loss. Book T calls it the Lord of Wealth, and Waite's additional note says it takes its value from the cards around it.

name: Page of Pentacles
upright: The Page of Pentacles is a student at heart. He's just been handed something, a job offer, a place on a course, a chance to learn a trade, and he's holding it up and studying it, working out how to make the most of it. This card is about diligence and practical ambition, the first real steps toward a goal you mean to see through. As a person, it's someone steady, earnest, and reliable, maybe a bit slow to get going but thorough once they do. Treat this small beginning like it matters, because it does. Start small and be consistent, since that's how the Page learns. One lesson a day adds up.
reversed: The plan stays a plan. The first step keeps getting put off, or you daydream about the goal without doing any of the work, or lose interest halfway through. Goals may be unrealistic, or a mistake keeps happening because nobody learned from it. News about work or money may also fall short of what you hoped. Pick the smallest real step and take it this week. Waite's reversed list includes wastefulness and luxury, so money meant for the plan may get spent on treats.
sitWith: What would it look like to take one small, practical step toward this? What do you want to learn, and what's the first lesson?
inASpread: Near the Eight of Pentacles or the Hierophant, the Page is a strong sign for study, training, or an apprenticeship. With the Ace of Pentacles, a new money or work opportunity is just beginning. The outcome here is slow, solid progress and a skill worth learning.
imagery: A young man stands in a green, flowering field with plowed land behind him, holding a pentacle up with both hands and studying it closely. He's just been handed something valuable and he's taking it seriously.

waite.upright: Application, study, scholarship, reflection; another reading says news, messages and the bringer thereof; also rule, management.
waite.reversed: Prodigality, dissipation, liberality. luxury; unfavourable news.
waite.picture: A youthful figure, looking intently at the pentacle which hovers over his raised hands. He moves slowly, insensible of that which is about him.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Youth holding a pentacle up to study it
symbols.meaning: Curiosity and focus on a practical goal, so absorbed he's insensible of what's around him.
Fertile ground where new learning can grow.
Knowledge that grows slowly over time.

symbols.symbol: Red cap with a long trailing cord
symbols.meaning: Enthusiasm and readiness to act.

history: The youth looks intently at a pentacle hovering over his raised hands, moving slowly and insensible of what is about him. Application, study, scholarship, and reflection are the chief meanings, with news and messages as another reading. His old Marseille title is Valet de Deniers, the page or knave of coins.
numerologyAstrology: Pages are the Earth part of their suit in Golden Dawn practice, so this is earth doubled: practical beginnings.

upright.love: A careful, sincere start, slower than some people like and very genuine. Interest shows up as practical gestures such as fixing your bike or remembering your schedule. A steady, sincere admirer may appear. Couples take practical steps together.
upright.work: A new course, an apprenticeship, or an entry-level job with real prospects. Waite's application and study fit someone ready to learn a trade properly. Training, a course, or a first job goes well. Take notes and ask questions.
upright.money: Good news about money, a small opportunity, or finally learning to budget. Start small and be consistent. A savings app that rounds up purchases suits this card. A free class on personal finance is worth the time.
upright.advice: Take the first real step and study what you're getting into. Diligence now pays off for years. Study and start small.
upright.asAPerson: Earnest, reliable, and eager to learn. Young or new to love, perhaps, and they mean what they say. Diligent, curious, and steady.

yesNo.why: It's a good start if the effort stays steady. Good news about money may be on the way.

reversed.love: Interest that never turns into action, or a partner who talks about plans and never makes them. Unfavourable news is one of the reversed meanings. Someone may talk about plans that never happen. Look for action behind words.
reversed.work: Procrastination, lost focus, or goals nobody could meet. The plan stays a plan until you break it into a first step. Procrastination stalls progress, so break the goal into small steps. Bad news may require a change of plan.
reversed.money: Wasteful spending on treats and trinkets. Waite gives prodigality, dissipation, and luxury, which is the student blowing the grant in a week. Small luxuries add up fast. Track spending for a week to see where it goes.
reversed.advice: Pick the smallest real step and take it this week. Stop researching and start doing. Tell someone what you'll finish by Friday.
reversed.asAPerson: Distracted, lazy, or careless with money. They may mean well and still not follow through. Distracted and wasteful.

yesNo.why: The work hasn't really started. The plan isn't moving yet.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists application (steady effort), study, scholarship, and reflection, and another reading gives news, messages, and “the bringer thereof”. He adds rule and management. In practice it's a student, a new skill, or a practical opportunity beginning.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives prodigality (wastefulness), dissipation, liberality (lavishness), luxury, and unfavourable news. In practice readers take it as a plan that stays a plan, poor focus, or money wasted.

imageryHistory: The Marseille-pattern Valet of Coins is a standing youth holding a coin. Smith drew a young man in a green field holding up a pentacle and studying it closely, with a ploughed field and trees behind him, the slow, absorbed figure Waite describes.

mathers.title: Knave of Pentacles
mathers.upright: A dark Youth, Economy, Order, Rule, Management
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: Princess of the Echoing Hills: Rose of the Palace of Earth
goldenDawn.printed: PRINCESS OF THE ECHOING HILLS: ROSE OF THE PALACE OF EARTH
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: A dark youth; a young officer or soldier; a child.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads a dark youth, economy, order, rule, and management, and reversed, prodigality, profusion, waste, and dissipation. Book T calls this court the Princess of the Echoing Hills.

name: Knight of Pentacles
upright: Slow and steady is the whole approach here. The Knight of Pentacles is hard work, routine, patience, and reliability, the person who shows up every day and finishes what he starts. Every other knight is charging somewhere, and this one is standing still, looking at the field he has to plow. That can be frustrating if you want quick results, but it's exactly how lasting things get built: saving a bit each month, going to the gym on the dull days, doing the job right. He's dependable, responsible, and not very exciting as a person, which is sometimes exactly what you need. Doing the boring thing every day is how the big thing gets done. Keep your routine and trust your pace.
reversed: Steady has turned into stuck. Boredom sets in with a routine that stopped serving you, or you've grown so cautious that you never take a single risk. For some it swings into workaholism, or into plain laziness, the horse that won't budge at all. Perfectionism shows up here too, being so careful that nothing ever gets finished. Change one small part of the routine and see if things start moving.
sitWith: Which boring, everyday habit would make the biggest difference if you kept it up? What routine would move you closer to your goal if you kept it every day?
inASpread: Next to the Knight or Eight of Wands, his slowness clashes with a situation that wants speed. With the Seven or Eight of Pentacles, it's all about patient effort that pays off eventually. Progress will be slow and certain if he's the final card.
imagery: A knight in dark armor sits still on a heavy black workhorse, holding a pentacle and looking at it, with neatly plowed fields stretching behind him. He's the only knight in the deck who isn't moving, and he's in no hurry at all.

waite.upright: Utility, serviceableness, interest, responsibility, rectitude—all on the normal and external plane.
waite.reversed: inertia, idleness, repose of that kind, stagnation; also placidity, discouragement, carelessness.
waite.picture: He rides a slow, enduring, heavy horse, to which his own aspect corresponds. He exhibits his symbol, but does not look therein.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Knight on a heavy black horse standing still
symbols.meaning: The slow, enduring, heavy horse: patience and reliability over speed.

symbols.symbol: Pentacle held out in his gloved hand
symbols.meaning: He shows his symbol but doesn't look into it, Waite says: duty more than vision.
Work waiting to be done, row by row.

symbols.symbol: Oak sprigs on his helmet and the horse's bridle
symbols.meaning: Endurance and slow, strong growth.

history: Waite describes him riding a slow, enduring, heavy horse to which his own aspect corresponds, and says he exhibits his symbol but does not look therein. Waite's meanings are utility, serviceableness, responsibility, and rectitude, all on the normal and external plane. His Sola Busca name is Sarafino.
numerologyAstrology: Knights are the Fire part of their suit in the Golden Dawn scheme, so this is fire of earth: steady effort pushed toward concrete goals.

upright.love: Slow, reliable love that proves itself over months. It may not be thrilling, and you can count on every word. Slow courtship suits this card, with someone reliable who takes their time. Couples build trust through consistent small acts.
upright.work: Routine, hard work, and finishing what you start. Waite's utility and responsibility describe the colleague everyone relies on. Showing up on time every day builds a reputation. See each task through to the end.
upright.money: Steady saving, careful investing, and income that grows slowly but surely. Patience builds wealth here. Paying down debt a little each month counts too. Stay with the plan you made. Automatic transfers into savings do the work for you.
upright.advice: Keep going one row at a time. Consistency beats speed on this field. Do the dull task first.
upright.asAPerson: Reliable, patient, hardworking, maybe a bit set in their ways. They show love by turning up every time.

yesNo.why: Slow and steady gets there. It will take longer than you'd like.

reversed.love: A relationship stuck in routine, or a partner who won't take the next step. Inertia, idleness, and stagnation are Waite's words for the reversal. Routine may have turned into a rut. Plan something new together.
reversed.work: Boredom, laziness, or perfectionism that stops anything from being finished. Change one small part of the routine to get moving again. Colleagues may be waiting on you without saying so. Set a deadline and stick to it.
reversed.money: Money sitting idle, or carelessness with bills. Waite includes discouragement and carelessness, so check what's been left undone. A late fee or lapsed insurance may be the first sign. Set up reminders for renewal dates.
reversed.advice: Shake up the routine a little. Stuck and steady look alike from a distance.
reversed.asAPerson: Stubborn, sluggish, or stuck in a rut. They may not budge however hard you push. Stuck and unmotivated.

yesNo.why: Things are stuck for the moment. Things are stalled right now.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists utility (usefulness), serviceableness, interest, responsibility, and rectitude (doing things properly), “all on the normal and external plane”, meaning practical and everyday. In practice it's hard work, routine, reliability, and slow steady progress.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives inertia, idleness, and “repose of that kind”, stagnation, placidity (too calm), discouragement, and carelessness. In practice readers take it as steady turned into stuck: boredom, laziness, or perfectionism.

imageryHistory: The Marseille-pattern Cavalier of Coins is a rider on horseback holding a coin. Smith drew him on a heavy black horse standing still in a ploughed field, holding a pentacle in his hand without looking at it, the slow, enduring rider Waite describes.

mathers.title: Knight of Pentacles
mathers.upright: A useful Man, Trustworthy, Wisdom, Economy, Order, Regulation
mathers.reversed: A brave Man, but out of Employment, Idle, Unemployed, Negligent.
mathers.source: S. L. MacGregor Mathers, The Tarot: Its Occult Signification, Use in Fortune-Telling, and Method of Play (1888)

goldenDawn.title: The Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land; the King of the Spirits of Earth
goldenDawn.printed: THE LORD OF THE WIDE AND FERTILE LAND; THE KING OF THE SPIRITS OF EARTH
goldenDawn.source: Golden Dawn "Book T", printed as "Liber LXXVIII: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot" in The Equinox I:8 (1912)

waiteAdditional.upright: An useful man; useful discoveries.
waiteAdditional.reversed: A brave man out of employment.
waiteAdditional.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), Part III section 4, "Some Additional Meanings of the Lesser Arcana"

olderMeanings.note: Mathers reads a useful man, trustworthy, wisdom, economy, order, and regulation, and reversed, a brave man out of employment, idle, unemployed, and negligent. Book T calls this court the Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land.

name: Queen of Pentacles
upright: The Queen of Pentacles is love in practical form. She's the one who makes sure everyone's fed, the bills are paid, and the house feels like home, and she's down to earth about all of it. She balances work and family, money and warmth, without making a fuss. She may be a real person, often a working mother or a generous friend, or your own ability to look after yourself and others in solid, everyday ways. Caring for someone can be as simple as a good meal and a warm blanket. Caring for others works best when you're cared for too. Make sure you're on your own list.
reversed: She's stretched too thin. Everyone's needs are getting met but yours, or you feel like you're failing at both work and home because there isn't enough of you to go around. Money worries may be part of it, or caring so much that it tips into control, doing everything for people instead of letting them do it themselves. Sometimes it's simpler: skipped meals, no sleep, a body running on fumes. The practical care you give others, you need too. Put your own needs back on the list.
sitWith: What practical kindness would you most like someone to do for you? How could you look after yourself as well as you look after others?
inASpread: With the Empress or the Queen of Cups, she brings a strong nurturing theme, often around home and family. In a spread heavy with Wands, she's the steadying hand that keeps things grounded. When she's the outcome, expect comfort, security, and practical support.
imagery: A queen sits on a throne carved with fruit and goat heads in a flowering garden, holding a pentacle in her lap and gazing down at it, while a small rabbit hops in the corner. She's surrounded by plenty, and she's looking after it with care.

waite.upright: Opulence, generosity, magnificence, security, liberty.
waite.reversed: Evil, suspicion, suspense, fear, mistrust.
waite.picture: The face suggests that of a dark woman, whose qualities might be summed up in the idea of greatness of soul; she has also the serious cast of intelligence; she contemplates her symbol and may see worlds therein.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Queen seated with a pentacle in her lap
symbols.meaning: She contemplates her symbol and may see worlds in it, as Waite says.
Beauty and abundance growing around her.
Fertility and the quiet plenty of the natural world.

symbols.symbol: Throne carved with fruit and goat heads
symbols.meaning: Earthly abundance and practical Capricorn strength.

history: Waite says her face suggests a dark woman whose qualities might be summed up in greatness of soul, with a serious cast of intelligence. The meanings he lists are opulence, generosity, magnificence, security, and liberty. Elena, Helen of Troy, is the Sola Busca name for the Queen of Coins.
numerologyAstrology: Queens are the Water part of their suit in the Golden Dawn scheme, so she is water of earth: care and nurture in practical form.

upright.love: Warm, practical love that feeds and shelters. A partner who makes a house feel like home, and who notices when you haven't eaten. Couples nurture each other in practical ways. Anyone dating may find someone warm and grounded.
upright.work: Balancing work and family well, or a nurturing role like managing, teaching, or care. Waite's security and generosity fit someone people lean on. Running a small business from the kitchen table suits you. People trust you.
upright.money: Comfort, wise spending, and generosity. Money used to look after people, including yourself. Spend wisely on comfort and care, and keep putting a little aside for security. A household fund for the unexpected keeps a warm home from turning into a worried one.
upright.advice: Look after yourself as well as you look after others. Practical care counts as love. Care for yourself too.
upright.asAPerson: Warm, generous, grounded, and capable. They want to take care of you and will show it in food, comfort, and help. Their home is usually where friends gather.

yesNo.why: Care and security favor this. Practical care says yes.

reversed.love: Care that tips into control, or neglecting yourself while everyone else is looked after. Suspicion, fear, and mistrust run through Waite's reversed meanings. Worry or control may creep into caring. Ask what the other person actually needs.
reversed.work: Stretched too thin between work and home, feeling like you're failing at both. Something needs to come off the list. Say no to one more task, and ask which duties could wait until next month. You can't pour from an empty cup.
reversed.money: Money worries, or spending to keep up appearances. One old note in Waite's book names an illness for the reversal, so health costs may be part of it. Money fears may cloud judgment. Look at the facts calmly.
reversed.advice: Put yourself back on the list. Nobody can keep a household running on an empty tank. Ease your grip.
reversed.asAPerson: Smothering, suspicious, or simply worn out. They may care too much and trust too little. Anxious and overextended.

yesNo.why: Fear or overwork gets in the way. Worry is clouding this.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists opulence, generosity, magnificence, security, and liberty. He describes her as having “greatness of soul” and “the serious cast of intelligence”. In practice she's practical love: someone who nurtures, provides, and makes a place feel like home.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives evil, suspicion, suspense, fear, and mistrust. In practice readers take it as care tipped into control or worry, self-neglect, or money fears.

imageryHistory: The Marseille-pattern Queen of Coins is a crowned queen seated with a coin. Smith seated her on a stone throne carved with fruit and goat heads in a flowering garden, holding a pentacle in her lap under an arch of roses, with a rabbit in the corner.

name: King of Pentacles
upright: The King of Pentacles has built something and it's paying off. He's the successful business owner, the steady provider, the person who made his money slowly and knows how to keep it. Grapes grow all over his robe and throne, and that's the point: his wealth is part of the ground he stands on. He's generous and reliable, happy to share advice or a helping hand, and he doesn't take silly risks. When he shows up, money and work are on solid footing, or you're being asked to handle them the way he would. Success built slowly is the kind that lasts. Share your know-how with someone starting out.
reversed: Money has become the whole story. He can turn greedy, stubborn, or obsessed with status, measuring everyone, himself included, by what they own. Bad financial decisions follow, a business going wrong, or someone who controls others with money. There's also the workaholic who has plenty and still can't stop grinding. Ask what all this is actually for. Money is a tool, and it shouldn't run the whole show.
sitWith: What would feel like enough, if you let it? What have you built that you're proud of, and how could you share it?
inASpread: The King of Pentacles next to the Emperor makes a strong picture of authority and material success. Paired with the Four of Pentacles or the Devil, his wealth has turned into greed. His answer as the final card is that your work will pay off in something solid and lasting. With the Ten of Pentacles, wealth passes down or lasts.
imagery: A king sits on a throne carved with bull heads, his robe covered in grapevines, holding a scepter and a pentacle, with a castle behind him and plants growing all around his feet. He's successful and comfortable, and his wealth is rooted in the land.

waite.upright: Valour, realizing intelligence, business and normal intellectual aptitude, sometimes mathematical gifts and attainments of this kind; success in these paths.
waite.reversed: Vice, weakness, ugliness, perversity, corruption, peril.
waite.picture: The figure calls for no special description; the face is rather dark, suggesting also courage, but somewhat lethargic in tendency. The bull's head should be noted as a recurrent symbol on the throne.
waite.source: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911)

symbols.symbol: Bull heads carved on the throne
symbols.meaning: A recurring symbol, Waite notes: Taurus and steady earthly strength.

symbols.symbol: Robe covered in grapes and vines
symbols.meaning: Wealth that grows from the ground he works.
What he has built and holds securely.

symbols.symbol: Sceptre in one hand, pentacle in the other
symbols.meaning: Authority and money used together.

history: The figure calls for no special description, Waite says, the face rather dark, suggesting courage but somewhat lethargic, and he points out the bull's head as a recurrent symbol on the throne. It is in this entry that Waite explains the suit stood for coins in many old packs, and that he did not invent the substitution of pentacles. The fifteenth-century Sola Busca deck calls its King of Coins Filipo, meaning Philip of Macedon, with an R for Rex.
numerologyAstrology: Kings are the Air part of their suit in the Golden Dawn scheme, so he is air of earth: clear judgment applied to material affairs.

upright.love: A steady provider and loyal partner who shows love through security and commitment. Not flashy, and completely dependable. Couples build a secure life together. A successful, generous suitor may turn up for someone single.
upright.work: Business success, leadership, and sound judgment. Waite's realizing intelligence and business aptitude, sometimes with a head for numbers. Business, finance, and leadership roles thrive. Trust experience.
upright.money: Wealth built steadily and managed well. A good time to invest, buy property, or ask an experienced person for financial advice. A mortgage, a business loan, or a pension decision goes well. Keep good records, since this king runs things properly.
upright.advice: Be the steady hand in the room. Use what you've built to support others. Build and share.
upright.asAPerson: Successful, reliable, generous, and practical, often a businessperson or someone in charge. They can offer real security. Many are business owners or managers with a steady routine.

yesNo.why: Sound judgment and resources favor this. Solid success says yes.

reversed.love: A partner who uses money to control, or one married to work. Vice, weakness, and corruption are Waite's reversed meanings. Expensive gifts may replace time together. Guard your evenings from the office, and talk about who decides on spending.
reversed.work: Greed, bad business decisions, or someone cutting ethical corners. Watch the person at the top. Bonuses tied to cutting corners are a warning sign. Protect your integrity. If you're asked to do something that feels wrong, get it in writing or refuse.
reversed.money: Poor investments, stubborn refusal to adapt, or wealth used badly. Get a second opinion before any big commitment. Stubborn decisions or bad investments may cost you. Check fees on any investment you haven't reviewed in years. Pride can keep you in a losing position too long.
reversed.advice: Ask what all this is actually for. Money is a tool, and it can't measure anyone's worth. Keep your integrity.
reversed.asAPerson: Greedy, stubborn, or status-obsessed, sometimes an old and vicious man in Waite's extra notes. They may measure you by what you have.

yesNo.why: Greed or poor judgment gets in the way. Greed spoils the answer.

waiteNote.upright: Waite lists valour, “realizing intelligence” (a mind that makes things happen), business and “normal intellectual aptitude”, and “sometimes mathematical gifts”, with success in these paths. He notes the bull's head as a recurring symbol on the throne. In practice it's business success, steady providing, and wealth built well.
waiteNote.reversed: Reversed, Waite gives vice, weakness, ugliness, perversity, corruption, and peril. In practice readers take it as greed, money used to control, or stubborn bad decisions.

imageryHistory: The Marseille-pattern King of Coins is a crowned king seated with a coin. Smith seated him on a throne carved with bull heads, his robe covered in grapevines, holding a sceptre and a pentacle, with a castle behind him and flowers at his feet.
